stem: An enterprise team is moving a SQL Server database to an open-source-compatible engine and wants its schema and stored procedures converted before any data moves, and separately is choosing an engine for a brand-new workload with no existing engine dependency that needs the highest throughput and read scaling available. Which TWO choices fit these two situations respectively? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Use AWS SCT to convert the schema and AWS DMS to migrate the data, for the SQL Server move
Choose Amazon Aurora for the new workload, compatible with either open-source SQL dialect
Use AWS DMS alone to convert the schema and migrate the data, for the SQL Server move
Choose Amazon RDS for SQL Server for the new workload, to stay compatible with T-SQL
Use AWS SCT alone to complete the entire SQL Server migration, including moving the data

rationale: Converting a SQL Server schema to an open-source engine is a heterogeneous migration, which needs AWS SCT for the schema and code and AWS DMS for the data; a brand-new workload with no existing engine dependency is exactly the case where Aurora's higher throughput and read scaling make it the default choice. AWS DMS does not convert schemas, so using it alone for the SQL Server move skips a required step. Choosing RDS for SQL Server for the new workload keeps a dependency the scenario says does not exist and gives up Aurora's throughput and replica scaling. AWS SCT converts schemas and code but does not move data, so it cannot complete the migration by itself.
